self.title: Flightdeck recording pipeline
self.caption: Flightdeck recording pipeline Collector macOS readings and process events. Scheduled once a second; measures source CPU cost. Shared-memory ring 120 tick slots plus a separate event log. One writer; readers can fall behind and lose overwritten records. Persister Separate process reads the ring, encodes bounded windows and commits them. Collection continues if it exits. Sealed recording Immutable Parquet windows of 60 elapsed seconds. Manifests retain availability, losses and clock bounds. Sealed recording → disk query API (implemented, not sampled here) → native viewer (not yet implemented). Planned live viewing also reads the ring. Neither path uses a metrics server or a dashboard service.

Leaders use component anchors; physical sensor coordinates and fan channel sides are unverified. CPU and GPU share the cooling assembly. The separate airflow colors are a display choice, not measured exhaust temperatures. Rotor and particle speed follows each channel’s RPM.

Apple’s 16-inch 2026 logic-board service view, fan procedure and exploded view establish the assembly layout: board and cooling assembly near the hinge, two blowers, six battery cells and side speaker assemblies. These references cover M5 Pro and M5 Max; this drawing simplifies the installed assembly.

CPU, GPU and memory leaders reference the covered processor assembly. Counterpoint’s M5 Pro chip teardown identifies separate CPU and GPU dies in one package, using a 14-inch machine. It does not establish their orientation in this 16-inch chassis. Individual memory and NAND outlines, sensor coordinates and fan-channel sides remain unverified.

These Apple references provide service illustrations. The current manual reuses 2024 detached-board and fan photos; iFixit also discloses earlier-model photos. Those photos support assembly context, not exact hidden M5 Pro chip placement. The 2026 installed locator anchors the major layout and cooling contour. No complete electrical schematic or sensor-coordinate map was verified in this research. Airflow is illustrative, not a measured path or speed.

packets: Packets are network messages counted across the measured interfaces. The plotted rate is packets per second (pps), derived from the dashboard counter over a 1-minute window.
Download is above zero; upload is mirrored below zero for separation. Inspected sent rates stay positive. This is packet count, not byte throughput.
errors: These rates count network receive/send errors or disk read/write errors per elapsed second, from the corresponding sysmon counters over a 1-minute window.
A measured zero means the source counted no errors in the interval. Unavailable readings and missing intervals remain distinct from zero.
openFiles: Open is the machine's reported number of open file entries. The dashed reference is the same count as a share of the reported system file limit, shown on a separate percentage axis.
These are system counters, not a count of the selected app's documents. Per-process open-file counts are available separately in app inspection.
pageDetail: Page-ins count memory pages brought in from disk, including app code, and are not limited to swap. Compressed/decompressed count the corresponding memory operations per second.
The dashboard counter rates use a 1-minute window. These event rates are distinct from compressed bytes in RAM and from swap byte throughput.
correlation: This overlay compares CPU and GPU utilization, whole-machine power, SoC temperature and fan speed at the same captured times. Power and temperature have separate labelled right axes; the dashed fan line uses an independent hidden rpm scale.
Temporal alignment helps you investigate a workload. It does not prove that one reading caused another; inspect app and process activity at the same captured instant.
gpu: GPU busy is the fraction of the measurement interval spent active. Active frequency is derived from cycles over active time and shown in GHz.
An interval with no usable active-time measurement has no meaningful frequency. Process GPU time is a separate measurement, available in the app breakdown.
gpuMemory: In-use and allocated memory are separate GPU-driver readings. They describe allocations in unified memory, not a second pool of physical RAM to add to the machine total.
Values are converted from bytes to GiB. The two lines are compared, not stacked or summed.
frequency: An effective clock frequency per CPU cluster, derived from measured cycles divided by active time. macOS changes clock states as the workload changes.
Shown in GHz. This is an interval measurement, not a fixed maximum clock or a performance score.
load: Work running or waiting for a CPU, averaged over 1, 5 and 15 minutes. The dashed reference marks 18 cores.
Core count is a rough reference on heterogeneous CPUs. Load is context, not a direct scheduler-delay measurement.
power: The system power sensor reports watts for the machine. The GPU series is its recorded energy per second. SoC and rest of system is calculated as the system reading minus that GPU rate; it is not an independently measured sensor.
The stacked component view sums to the system reading where both inputs are available. Process-attributed energy rates have a separate scope; they are not exact shares of the system sensor.
fan: A fan tachometer measures rotation in revolutions per minute. It does not measure temperature. This snapshot retains fan channels 0 and 1 separately.
Fan histories are on Energy. The Overview schematic shows both channels; their physical left/right assignments remain unverified.
snapshot: This prototype embeds a captured hour from your local sysmon dashboard. Every plot, ranking and selected value uses that same time range. The page does not follow the live machine.

Samples are 30 seconds apart; counter rates use 1-minute windows. Candidate app histories retain the top ten at every sampled instant and the top eight averages for the two displayed ranges. Process-group detail is included for 12 apps. This demonstrates the intended interface, not a completed native Flightdeck app.
cpu: Whole-machine CPU utilization uses all 18 cores as 100%. A cluster chart uses that cluster's capacity. Process and app CPU use one core as 100%, so their values can exceed 100%.
Source: sysmon CPU scheduler counters. Rates use a 1-minute window. Compare resource activity at the same instant; alignment alone does not prove causation.
pressure: The bars compare measured CPU-cluster, GPU and memory utilization against their own stated capacities. Memory pressure and thermal state are macOS verdicts, shown separately as named states.
Memory pressure is not calculated from swap or compression. Only a critical thermal state means heat is reducing performance.
appCpu: CPU time is grouped by app, including its related processes. Here 100% is one CPU core. The full machine has 18 cores; kernel work and attribution boundaries mean app totals need not match whole-machine utilization exactly.

The top eight average app series are selected for the displayed interval; Other includes the remaining app readings. The dashed All CPU reference sums recorded machine CPU busy-time rates in one-core percentage units.
appMemory: Resident memory counts RAM attributed to processes. Shared pages count in more than one process, so app resident totals can exceed physical memory. They are not a partition of the 48 GiB installed.
The machine's used-memory reading is a separate measurement. App charts preserve the grouped process readings and do not force them to add up to physical memory.
appNetwork: Traffic rates group the received and sent bytes attributed to an app's processes. The machine's interface total is a separate measurement.
Values use decimal MB/s and 1-minute rate windows. Top app bars are scaled to the largest app in the panel, not to a hardware capacity.
appDisk: Read and write byte rates grouped by app. Compare an app's activity with machine throughput and operations at the same captured time.
Values use decimal MB/s and 1-minute rate windows. App attribution and device counters are different sources.
appGpu: Recorded GPU time per elapsed interval, grouped by app. This is a process-time measurement, not a direct partition of whole-GPU busy time.
The machine's GPU busy percentage is shown separately. Summed process GPU time should not be treated as a utilization ceiling.
appEnergy: The rate of recorded process energy, grouped by app, in joules per second or watts. It differs from measured whole-machine power.
Process-energy attribution and the machine's power sensor have different scopes. These values do not divide the whole-machine reading into exact shares.
memory: Used memory combines the app, wired and compressed categories used by your sysmon dashboard. Pressure is macOS's separate verdict. Compression and swap can remain in use at normal pressure.
The quantity panels show source counters independently. They are not a claim that app resident-memory totals partition physical RAM.
storage: Throughput is bytes per second; operations are completed requests per second. Reported mean I/O time divides the source disk-time counter by completed operations, in milliseconds.

These are machine-wide captured device counters, not per-process request latency. The source mean cannot establish queue wait or latency percentiles. Mirrored write rates remain positive in inspection; undefined readings stay unavailable.
network: Received and sent interface bytes over elapsed time. The app breakdown groups process-attributed traffic, so its scope differs from the machine's interface counters.
Decimal MB/s, with 1-minute windows. Upload is mirrored below zero for separation; the inspected sent rate stays positive. A missing source value is not a measured zero.
thermal: Temperature-area histories show the hottest measured sensor in each source group. CPU, GPU, memory and storage temperatures are on their resource pages; Energy holds the remaining groups and fan histories.

The source SoC group average is separate from its maximum. Area readings do not locate individual sensors. Fan RPM measures rotation, not temperature; macOS thermal state is an independent system verdict.
battery: Battery charge is relative to reported full capacity. Health compares full-charge capacity with design capacity. Signed battery power is positive into the battery and negative while discharging.
Source: sysmon battery-controller readings. Adapter rating is a separate limit, not a measurement of current system power.
process: The sysmon dashboard groups processes by their reported name inside the selected app. A row may represent several process instances; it is not a PID or a unique process creation.
This snapshot includes process-group readings for 12 apps. Flightdeck's actual historical viewer still needs its own complete process identity and availability contract.
memoryComposition: App, wired and compressed memory are the categories included in the machine’s used-memory reading. Cached and free memory are listed separately.
The installed line marks physical capacity. Independently rounded captured categories can differ slightly from the used total. This is separate from process resident memory and from macOS pressure.
gpuPower: Recorded GPU energy divided by elapsed time, expressed in watts.
This is a component reading, not whole-machine power or per-process attribution. No CPU or Neural Engine power is supplied by this capture.
selfMonitoring: This page uses a saved five-minute Flightdeck collector/persister diagnostic run. The native viewer now exists; this older capture did not measure it. No live Flightdeck telemetry is connected to this saved diagnostic page.

Times are elapsed from run start. Ten-second collector reports, one-minute CPU/memory observations and completed seals have different scopes. This run is not time-aligned with the sysmon machine snapshot. Uncaptured signals remain unavailable.
